metric.build_test_integration.evidence_sources_and_retrieval_route: Web search (provider-brokered) against official docs (turbo.build, vitest.dev) and current third-party tooling comparison articles dated 2026; same retrieval route and examination depth applied as would be applied to other languages in this metric family.

citations: Compare tsup, unbuild, pkgroll, tsc, esbuild, and SWC for building TypeScript libraries and applications in 2026.
esbuild is 45x faster than tsc for transpilation.
bundler_ecosystem_breadth.note: Rich, actively benchmarked set of TypeScript-aware build tools (esbuild, swc, tsup, unbuild, webpack, Vite, Rollup) each with defined roles for libraries vs applications.

citations: Turborepo is a high-performance monorepo build tool that simplifies dependency management and speeds up builds through caching.
Nx offers a highly integrated monorepo experience, by implementing an efficient caching mechanism, storing results from previous executions.
monorepo_orchestration.note: Turborepo and Nx are established, actively documented monorepo build systems with caching, parallelization, and TypeScript-specific configuration guides.

citations: For Internal Packages, we recommend that you use tsc to compile your TypeScript libraries whenever possible.
tsc: Only tool that performs type checking; transpilation is 45x slower than esbuild
official_build_tool.note: tsc is the reference compiler for both type-checking and emission, with incremental/composite project-reference builds; official monorepo guidance recommends tsc for internal packages.

citations: Vitest offers the best out-of-the-box TypeScript support via Vite.
Out-of-box ESM, TypeScript and JSX support powered by Oxc.
test_framework_native_integration.note: Vitest provides out-of-the-box TypeScript transpilation with no separate ts-jest/Babel config, while Jest remains viable via ts-jest/@swc/jest; both are mature, well-documented paths.

metric.build_test_integration.limitations: Sub-scores are worker-assigned integer estimates within each 25-point rubric band, informed by cited evidence rather than a single numeric benchmark; identical band definitions and evidence-collection depth are intended to be applied to every language under this metric.
rubric_components_equal_weight_25pts_eac: Official/standard compiler-driven build tooling: incremental builds, project references, watch mode
Native or near-native test-framework integration with the language/build system (minimal transform friction)
Breadth/maturity of surrounding build-tool ecosystem (bundlers/transpilers) that plug into the language's build pipeline
Monorepo/large-project build orchestration (caching, parallelization, workspace-awareness) and CI-friendliness

metric.documentation_quality.evidence_sources_and_retrieval_route: Web search (provider-brokered) against typescriptlang.org, tsdoc.org, microsoft/tsdoc and TypeStrong/typedoc GitHub repos, and DefinitelyTyped project pages; same retrieval route and examination depth applied as for other languages in this metric family.

citations: DefinitelyTyped is a community-led open-source repository for TypeScript type definitions.
DefinitelyTyped is one of the largest repositories on GitHub, with over 8,000 packages typed by thousands of contributors.
community_ecosystem_openness.note: DefinitelyTyped is a large, actively maintained community documentation/typing repository feeding inline docs and type information for thousands of packages, with an automated publishing pipeline.

citations: In the screenshot, we can see now that we have TSDoc comments in our editor and hints highlighting detail about the API of our method.
ide_integration.note: TSDoc-annotated comments surface directly as editor hints/tooltips (e.g., in VS Code), giving inline documentation without leaving the editor.

citations: The TypeScript Handbook is intended to be a comprehensive document that explains TypeScript to everyday programmers.
The reference section below the handbook in the navigation is built to provide a richer understanding of how a particular part of TypeScript works.
The TypeScript docs are an open source project.
official_handbook_reference.note: The official Handbook is explicitly scoped as a comprehensive, readable introduction plus a deeper reference section, maintained as an open-source project.

citations: TSDoc is a spec maintained by the TypeScript team.
TypeDoc is an open-source project that uses TSDoc to generate API documentation.
TSDoc is a proposal to standardize the doc comments used in TypeScript code, so that different tools can extract content without getting confused by each other's markup.
standardized_doc_comment_tooling.note: TSDoc is a spec maintained by the TypeScript team specifically to standardize doc comments across tools, with TypeDoc as a widely used generator and an official reference implementation package.

metric.documentation_quality.limitations: Sub-scores are worker-assigned integer estimates within each rubric band informed by cited evidence; DefinitelyTyped size figures vary across sources and are used only as one qualitative signal among several, not as a standalone popularity proxy.

rubric_components.component: Official comprehensive documentation (handbook/reference covering fundamentals and configuration)
Standardized doc-comment format and tooling for API doc generation
Community documentation ecosystem, openness and currency
